meta.framing: These are candidate signal generators for originating NFL prices. A strategy is a hypothesis plus a test, not a tip. No edge, win rate, ROI or confidence number is asserted anywhere in this catalogue, because no price data exists in this repo to compute them from; edge_claim is null on purpose and stays null until a gate run produces a number.

inputs_legend.verified-available: read from an official source in this session
inputs_legend.available-not-yet-wired: official source identified, ingestion not built

meta.example_policy: The Week 10 example on each strategy uses only the captured official availability snapshot. It reports the signal value. It never reports a price, a side to take, or an expected return, because the market side of the comparison does not exist here.

strategies.name: Availability delta vs price staleness
strategies.hypothesis: When a club's availability changes after its price was set (late Out designation, IR move, confirmed backup QB), the market reprices unevenly: fast on the spread, slow on team totals and on the opposite side of the same stat family.
strategies.signal: delta_avail = availability_score(A) - availability_score(B) computed at T; compare against the *same* market's price at T-24h. Bet only where the score moved materially and the price did not, on a market type whose repricing lag is measured, not assumed.
strategies.availability_score_definition: Position-weighted replacement gap (SG-05). Until the ladder is estimated, the honest proxy is count of Out+Doubtful, reported with its known weakness.
strategies.entry: From the last mandatory filing to 20 minutes before lock; never before the Friday report on a Sunday game.
strategies.no_bet: If the market's own move already exceeds our estimated impact; if the news confidence label is 'report:'; if the bettor's book did not post the pre-news price (no stale line to beat).
strategies.stake_rule: 0.25x Kelly capped at the config limit; one bet per game per market family.
strategies.targets: Whether a *lag* exists at all. Phase 1 of this strategy is a measurement of lag per market type, not a betting system.
strategies.why_real: Availability is public, unevenly attended, and mechanically tied to lineup construction; small and mid-market books have fewer staff to reprice every team-total derivative after a late Out.
strategies.how_it_loses: Everyone else sees the same headline; the stale line is stale because it is limit-capped and unreachable at size; and the count-based score mistakes a 4th-string long snapper for a starting cornerback.
strategies.week10_example: SEA: 4 players Out (QB1 with ribs/quadricep, LT, two interior linemen...) vs LV: 0 Out / 0 Doubtful. Availability delta is large and one-directional, and the league's own report confirms the Seahawks' starting QB changed (no designation, will start - the named replacement). Signal fires on SEA-side team totals and on any market that priced SEA before Thursday. No price to compare against exists here, so the recorded output is 'directional flag, unpriced'.

strategies.name: Trench depletion -> rush-attempt suppression
strategies.hypothesis: Availability loss concentrated on the offensive line (centre/guards/tackles Out) suppresses called rushing volume and increases negative-down pass frequency more than the spread reflects.
strategies.signal: line_value_gap = weighted Out/Doubtful count among T/G/C positions; fire when >= 2 starters-or-next-up are unavailable and the team's called rush rate was already below league median.
strategies.entry: Pre-lock, after the last report; skip if the team's backup centre is a previously starting player (replacement quality, not count).
strategies.no_bet: No-bet when line play is unlisted (a blank in the report is not a healthy O-line); no-bet in the first week after a coordinator change.
strategies.stake_rule: flat 1u in research; fractional Kelly once a lag estimate exists.
strategies.targets: An availability-to-playcalling pathway that is testable with box-score-level data only.
strategies.why_real: Offensive-line availability is the least glamorous coverage area and the most mechanically linked to a specific, separately-priced derivative.
strategies.how_it_loses: Coaches compensate with quick game and the called-rush number barely moves; a 2nd-string tackle season is already in the season-long number so there is nothing left to price.
strategies.blocked_on: Q-MKT-03 (are team totals/rush props priced and archived?)
strategies.week10_example: Teams with >= 2 OL/interior linemen Out in the verified snapshot: NE (C Out), DET (C Out), KC (T Out), GB (C Out), TEN (G Out), IND (T Out + 2 others), NO (T Out, C Out), HOU (G Out), LAR (G Out), AZ (C Out, G Out), SEA (T Out, G Out). This is the candidate set. No priced conclusion is claimed.

strategies.name: Quarterback-chain collapse (QB2/QB3 starts)
strategies.hypothesis: A confirmed non-first-string starting QB moves a game more than the spread shows, because the spread absorbs the plan change (shorter passes, more run) while the total and the opponent's pass-attack props absorb very little of it.
strategies.signal: confirmed_start(QB depth index > 1) from club-official or league confirmation only - never from a 'report:' item; then evaluate which markets did and did not reprice.

inputs.name: QB depth per club, current week

strategies.entry: Only after a confirmation, and only where the pre-confirmation price is still obtainable.
strategies.no_bet: Rest/no-designation ambiguity; a QB returning from IR with 1+ prior starts that season (not a true chain collapse); dome games where the effect compresses.
strategies.stake_rule: half the size of an equivalent S-01 bet: same news family, correlated exposure.
strategies.targets: Whether second-derivative markets (totals, opponent props) lag the primary market after a QB change.
strategies.why_real: Two independent items in the Week 10 capture show confirmed backup starts in the same week (CLE and AZ), and a third where a QB1 was ruled out mid-week (SEA). The pattern is frequent enough to study.
strategies.how_it_loses: Books price backup QBs with a large, well-researched penalty already; the 'lag' is a rounding error and the vig eats it.
strategies.week10_example: Verified from the official report page's news list: SEA QB1 Out (ruled out) with the replacement confirmed to start; CLE named a non-first-string starter vs HOU; AZ named a different starter vs LAR. BAL's franchise QB was reported out 6-10 weeks with the backup QB also reported out for the season, i.e. a third-string situation in the same slate. Frequency: this is not a rare regime.

strategies.name: Late-inactive harvest (beat the stale close)
strategies.hypothesis: Some prices set before the last mandatory filing remain obtainable for minutes after the inactive list is known. The edge is defined by the difference to the close, and it is measurable on the very first weekend.
strategies.signal: price_taken vs price_at_close on the anchor, per bet; the *product* is a measurement of how many minutes of exploitable window exist per book.
strategies.entry: Only within the post-inactive window; any bet placed earlier belongs to S-01, not here.
strategies.no_bet: No-bet where the book limits winners quickly (this strategy's real cost is account limits, not variance).
strategies.stake_rule: flat, deliberately small: this is a data-collection strategy that occasionally pays.
strategies.targets: Whether we can beat the close at all. If we cannot, no model in this catalogue should be trusted with capital.
strategies.why_real: Widely accepted in principle; the disagreement is about size and durability, which is exactly what measurement settles.
strategies.how_it_loses: The window is seconds; the fill is rejected; the close we beat was at another book that never gives us that price at size.

strategies.name: Short week / rest asymmetry
strategies.hypothesis: A team on three days' rest, or crossing time zones, or playing an early international kickoff, shows a late-game production pattern that totals and second-half markets underprice.
strategies.signal: rest_days < 4 OR international_venue OR kickoff_local_time in [06:00,11:00]; combine with availability delta so fatigue and depletion are not double counted.
strategies.no_bet: Where the rest asymmetry is already public knowledge two weeks ahead (Thursday games are priced for it) - test whether any residual exists before betting.
strategies.targets: The residual after the obvious part is priced.
strategies.why_real: Week 10 contains a genuine instance: an international game at 9:30 AM ET with one club coming off a 5-4 season and the other resting a week longer than usual.
strategies.how_it_loses: Everyone has known since the schedule was announced; there is no new information at bet time, only a story.
strategies.week10_example: Verified from the official schedule page: NE at DET, Sunday 15 November, 9:30 AM ET, listed as 'International Game, Munich', on FOX. That single fixture legitimately triggers this strategy's condition; it also triggers its 'priced weeks in' veto. Both are recorded, and the veto is the default.

strategies.name: Weather-conditioned totals (wind and roof)
strategies.hypothesis: Wind at open-air venues moves scoring more than temperature does, and the market reacts to temperature headlines while under-reacting to the wind forecast that actually matters.
strategies.signal: sustained wind + gusts at kickoff window from an official meteorological source, joined to roof status; fire on the total only when the forecast moved materially within the last 24h.
strategies.entry: On forecast revision events, not on a schedule.
strategies.no_bet: Dome games; roofs that are decision-dependent on game-day operations rather than forecast; any model that reads a re-forecast instead of the archived forecast.
strategies.stake_rule: flat 1u; cap two weather bets per week (shared driver = G-8).
strategies.targets: Whether wind has residual explanatory power after the market's own move.
strategies.why_real: Forecast updates are public, timestamped, and mechanically predictive of deep-passing efficiency.
strategies.how_it_loses: Books use the same forecast feed at the same second; the trade is a race we lose.

strategies.name: Defensive-back-seven depletion vs opponent pass volume
strategies.hypothesis: Losing multiple interior defensive linemen/linebackers raises opponent pass-attempt volume (more third-and-long converted to neutral, more negative game scripts) more reliably than it raises points, so it is better expressed in volume markets than on the spread.
strategies.signal: count Out/Doubtful among DT/DE/LB grouped by role; require >= 2 AND that the replacement is a rotation/next-up player rather than a starter.
strategies.no_bet: No-bet when game script dominates (heavy favourite at home), or when the depletion is 'rest' rather than injury - the Week 10 report literally contains 'Not injury related - resting player' rows that must not be counted as lost quality for next week.
strategies.targets: Volume-vs-score separation, a claim that can be tested with box-score data before any money moves.
strategies.why_real: Availability rows are unambiguous about position; the market's pricing of 'who is missing' is where the effort goes, not 'what it changes next down'.
strategies.how_it_loses: Attempts are noise; completion rates collapse; the volume market is thin and vig-heavy so the edge is eaten.
strategies.week10_example: Two rows in the verified snapshot show 'Not injury related - resting player' with an Out designation on the same club's defensive front (JAX, both S and DT). Under a count-based model that is 2 units of defensive depletion. Under a correct model it is 0 for next week and a small positive for this week. This is the clearest available demonstration of why a rest flag must be separated from an injury flag before any counting is trusted.

strategies.name: Usage-reallocation prop ladder
strategies.hypothesis: When a lead ball-carrier or WR1 is Out, the replacement's usage line moves later and less than the reallocation of touches/targets; the correct bet is usually the *second* option, not the headline replacement.
strategies.signal: for each unavailable skill player, compute expected snap/target/rush share reallocation to teammates by depth order; compare to the movement in teammates' lines; fire where a teammate's line did not move at all.
strategies.entry: Pre-lock; props are void-prone so require a post-lock re-check of the inactive list.
strategies.no_bet: Any backfield with a committee already; any team whose game script is a >10-point favourite (rush attempts collapse); any prop whose line was never re-offered after news.
strategies.stake_rule: half size vs a main-market bet; max 2 legs from the same game.
strategies.targets: Whether reallocation is systematically underpriced one level below the replacement.
strategies.why_real: Books reprice the famous name; the second name has less attention and a thinner limit, and the reallocation is nearly deterministic.
strategies.how_it_loses: Prop lines are repriced instantly by an algorithm on the same input; and the 'reallocation' is offset by a game script the market already priced.
strategies.blocked_on: Q-ROSTER-03 (snap data licence), SG-17 descope decision
strategies.week10_example: Verified snapshot contains a franchise RB Out (GB, finger) and a starting RB Out (NO, shoulder) with the same club losing a second RB to Doubtful. A reallocation model would look at the *next* back on each depth chart; the site cannot name them, because depth-chart data is not available here - that missing cell is the point.

strategies.name: Correlated same-game parlay, priced on measured dependence
strategies.hypothesis: Same-game parlays are priced as if legs were independent; for legs that share a game script, the true joint probability is higher than the product, so a small number of well-chosen pairs are less vig-burdened than the singles.
strategies.signal: select leg pairs whose *measured* joint-settlement excess is positive and whose combined vig is below the singles' combined vig; only pairs above the sample minimum are priced.
strategies.entry: Pre-lock only; never live for this strategy (live correlation structure differs).
strategies.no_bet: Any pair with no measured correlation (hard refusal - this is the whole discipline of the strategy); any pair whose legs share a void rule that can kill both at once.
strategies.stake_rule: count as one unit of exposure against both legs' markets for G-8 caps.
strategies.targets: Whether the parlay vig discount genuinely exceeds the correlation adjustment.
strategies.why_real: Arithmetic: a parlay of two -110 legs implies roughly +240 while the true joint price with positive dependence can be shorter than that.
strategies.how_it_loses: The dependence is negative in the tail (a blowout kills both the 'over' legs), the pair never accumulates enough observations, or the book's parlay engine already models the dependence.

strategies.name: Anti-correlated prop pair (insurance structure)
markets: player over + player under on opposite-impact props
strategies.hypothesis: Some prop pairs are negatively correlated (a team's pass attempts over vs its rush attempts over). Pairs priced independently by the book create a structure whose cost is below the fair price of the pair, and can be used to keep an exposure alive through a game-script flip.
strategies.signal: find pairs whose measured joint loss probability is below the product of marginals by more than the combined vig.
strategies.no_bet: Never use to rescue a losing position (the common degenerate use); no-bet if the pair's purpose is not stated in the pre-registered hypothesis.
strategies.targets: Whether hedge structures survive vig, which is usually no.
strategies.why_real: Structural, not predictive: it relies on the book pricing legs independently in a thin market.
strategies.how_it_loses: The combined vig exceeds the dependence benefit - this is the base case, which is why the gate is 'measure first, price never without it'.

strategies.name: Cross-market internal consistency (the market's own line)
strategies.hypothesis: Side, total and moneyline jointly imply a score distribution; when they are mutually inconsistent, the inconsistency is either our parsing error or a real dislocation, and either answer is worth knowing.
strategies.signal: reconstruct implied win probability from (spread, total) and compare with the moneyline's implied probability, per book; flag disagreement beyond a tolerance calibrated to the book's own vig.
strategies.entry: Only on simultaneous snapshots - a 30-second-old spread against a fresh total produces false alarms.
strategies.no_bet: Every 'dislocation' that is explained by half-point asymmetry or by hold placed unevenly on purpose.
strategies.stake_rule: flat, capped; this is a data-quality tool first.
strategies.targets: Whether the book's prices are internally coherent enough to define a 'fair' baseline we can deviate from.
strategies.why_real: It requires no forecast at all, only simultaneous prices, so it is the cheapest genuine test of whether this environment can ever originate a line.
strategies.how_it_loses: Nothing wins here directly; it fails only by consuming engineering time that should have gone to SG-01.

strategies.name: Pure line-shopping baseline (the strategy to beat)
strategies.hypothesis: Taking the best available price across N books, with no view at all, generates positive CLV. This is the null model the whole catalogue must out-perform.
strategies.signal: always take max(price) across books at bet time; no model.

inputs.name: N books' prices at the same second

strategies.no_bet: n/a - nothing to get wrong; the risk is a false sense of edge that ignores limits.
strategies.targets: The floor: if a strategy's CLV <= S-12's CLV, it adds no information.
strategies.how_it_loses: Winners get limited, so the shopping edge decays for the account that needs it most.
strategies.notes: Kept on the leaderboard as a benchmark entry by policy (SG-13).

strategies.name: Two-sided fair-value origination engine
strategies.hypothesis: A genuine 'line we originate' requires a state-space team-strength model that updates on availability and play-calling inputs, then outputs a distribution of margins; the market comparison then tells us where our uncertainty is largest rather than where our opinion is loudest.
strategies.signal: fit margin and total distributions (schedule-adjusted, opponent-corrected, availability-conditioned); output (mu, sigma); quote spread = -mu with vig, and post our own price on a two-sided venue only where sigma is small.

inputs.name: an outlet that lets us post a price

strategies.entry: Originating a price is a market-making activity, not a taker activity: it requires venue access, which is an unresolved reviewer decision.
strategies.no_bet: Do not originate where our sigma is large (injury-driven uncertainty) - quoting wide is not the same as quoting well.
strategies.targets: The brief's headline ask. This entry exists to state plainly that origination is a venue/counterparty problem before it is a modelling problem.
strategies.why_real: The modelling half is tractable with data we can already verify; the venue half is the gate.
strategies.how_it_loses: We become the slow book: sharps take only our bad prices. Adverse selection is the default outcome of quoting without an information advantage.

strategies.name: Reverse line movement / sharp-flow detection
strategies.hypothesis: Price moving against public ticket pressure indicates informed flow. Where the public side is also the soft book's side, following the move is +CLV.
strategies.signal: delta_price(anchor) vs delta_tickets(slow book), sign mismatch of magnitude >= threshold, within a fixed window before lock.
strategies.entry: Only in the last window before lock, when there is no time left for the move to be retraced.
strategies.no_bet: No-bet where the 'public' number is unavailable (this rule depends on data most setups do not have); no-bet on obvious steam that is 45 minutes old.
strategies.targets: Whether price direction carries information beyond our own model's view.
strategies.why_real: Widely used; contested; cheap to test once price streams exist.
strategies.how_it_loses: The move was the soft book following us, and we then pay for a price we caused.

strategies.name: Report-trajectory classifier (practice-to-status transition)
strategies.hypothesis: The weekly pattern of a designation (DNP -> Limited -> Full, or the reverse) carries information about game participation that the final Friday label alone discards. Predicting participation well is upstream of every availability strategy.
strategies.signal: transition features over the Mon-Wed-Thu-Fri reports for the same player and week; output P(plays), calibrated; use it to convert Questionable rows into probabilities instead of dropping them.
strategies.entry: Not a betting strategy; a component. Scored on calibration, never on PnL.
strategies.targets: Turning the biggest known noise source (Questionable) into a usable probability.
strategies.why_real: The label is a club's expectation filed under a league policy; expectation has structure, and the same club files every week.
strategies.how_it_loses: Designations are gameable by the filer; a classifier learns a team's communication style, not football truth - which still predicts, but only until the team changes its habits.

strategies.name: Depth-chain quality monitor (the brief's 'backups replacing starters' ask)
strategies.hypothesis: The useful quantity is not 'who is out' but 'how far down the depth chart does this injury push the unit', which requires a per-unit starter/next-up/after-that chain and the quality gap between the links.
strategies.signal: for each unit (OL, DL, LB, CB, WR, backfield), build chain = [starter, next-up, after-that] with availability status per link; report chain_shift_depth (how many links the unit moved down) and gap_quality (unmeasured until a replacement-value estimate exists).

inputs.name: snap counts to derive chains retrospectively

strategies.targets: The missing object in the whole brief. Everything else in the availability family is downstream of it.
strategies.why_real: Verified by inspection: the official report page in this snapshot has columns for Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status, Game Status - and nothing about the replacement. The gap is structural, so it must be sourced, never derived from that page.
strategies.how_it_loses: If depth charts are unofficial, they are wrong on exactly the weeks that matter (after trades and IR moves - both occurred in this snapshot).
